text: Meanwhile Saul, still breathing out murderous threats against the Lord's disciples, went to the high priest
and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any there who followed the Way, men or women, he could bring them bound to Jerusalem.
As he traveled and was nearing Damascus, suddenly a light from the sky flashed all around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?
Who are you, Lord? he asked. I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting, the voice replied.
Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.
The men traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the sound but seeing no one.
Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could see nothing, so they led him by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he was blind, and he neither ate nor drank.
Now there was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord spoke to him in a vision: Ananias! Here I am, Lord, he answered.
The Lord told him, Get up and go to the street called Straight, and ask at Judas's house for a man from Tarsus named Saul, who is praying there right now.
He has seen in a vision a man named Ananias come in and lay hands on him to restore his sight.
But Lord, Ananias answered, I've heard from many people about all the harm this man has done to your saints in Jerusalem,
and he's here with authority from the chief priests to arrest everyone who calls on your name.
The Lord told him, Go anyway, for this man is my chosen instrument to carry my name before Gentiles, kings, and the people of Israel.
I myself will show him how much he must suffer for my name's sake.

So Ananias went and entered the house, and laying his hands on Saul, said, Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road you were traveling, has sent me so you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
At once something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized,
and after eating some food he regained his strength. Saul stayed several days with the disciples in Damascus.
Right away he began preaching in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.
Everyone who heard him was amazed and asked, Isn't this the man who wrecked those who called on this name in Jerusalem, and came here specifically to bring them bound before the chief priests?
But Saul kept growing more capable, and baffled the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Messiah.
After quite some time had passed, the Jews plotted together to kill him,
but Saul learned of their scheme. They watched the city gates around the clock, intending to kill him,
but his disciples took him one night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the wall.
When he reached Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples there, but they were all afraid of him, not believing he was really a disciple.

Barnabas, though, took him and brought him to the apostles, explaining how Saul had seen the Lord on the road and that the Lord had spoken to him, and how boldly he had preached in Jesus' name at Damascus.
So Saul stayed with them, moving freely about Jerusalem and speaking out boldly in the Lord's name.
He also spoke and debated with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they kept trying to kill him.
When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
Meanwhile the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria enjoyed a season of peace and was strengthened. Living in reverence for the Lord and encouraged by the Holy Spirit, it continued to grow.
As Peter traveled from place to place, he also came down to visit the believers living in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas, paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
Peter said to him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed. And immediately he got up.
All who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
Now in Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, which translates to Dorcas. She was always doing good deeds and giving to those in need.
About that time she grew sick and died; after washing her body, they laid her in an upstairs room.
Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing Peter was there, sent two men urging him, Please come to us without delay.

So Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they brought him to the upstairs room, where all the widows stood around him weeping, showing him the tunics and garments Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
Peter sent everyone out of the room, then knelt down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, Tabitha, get up. She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, sat up.
He took her by the hand and helped her stand, then called the saints and widows in and presented her alive.
News of this spread throughout Joppa, and many put their faith in the Lord.
Peter stayed on in Joppa for quite a while, lodging with a tanner named Simon.
